description: Adds an Arvo Part style harmony note to a melody by picking a note out of a reference chord, and can also be used as a chord quantizer

params.text: Chooses how the harmony note is picked: Up, the next chord note above the melody; Down, the next below; Up+1 and Down-1, the second; Up/Down and Up+1/Down-1 alternate; Quantize, the nearest
Shifts the harmony note by up to three octaves either way from the melody

inputs.text: The notes making up the reference chord, 1V per octave, one per channel; the chord is laid out over one octave and repeated across the whole range, so any tuning can be used
The melody to harmonise, 1V per octave, one note per polyphonic channel
In the alternating modes, a trigger here flips the harmony between upwards and downwards; it can be left unpatched in the other modes

outputs.text: The melody and its harmony together, 1V per octave, two channels for each channel of the melody: the melody note first, then its harmony note
The harmony notes, 1V per octave, one channel for each channel of the melody

notes: with nothing patched to the chord jack the module has no notes to harmonise with and the harmony output stays at 0V
Aaron Static's ChordCV produces a chord signal of the right shape
melody voltages are held between -10V and 10V before use
